description: Trigger and behavior cases for prompt-injection defense: trust zones, the untrusted-content invariant, deterministic action boundary as primary control, indirect-injection handling, red-team suite, manual-only.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke prompt-injection-defender. Harden our email-triage agent against prompt injection. It reads incoming emails and can archive, label, and forward them. Emails are obviously attacker-controlled.

assertions: Maps trust zones and states the invariant that email content (untrusted) cannot change instructions, tool permissions, identity, policy, or plan.

Makes the deterministic action boundary the primary control: forward/archive/label authorized by code against the user's permissions, with irreversible actions approval-gated, so a successful injection still cannot cause harm.
Handles indirect injection explicitly (the payload lives in the email body) and labels delimiting/detection as cost-raising, not sufficient alone.
Designs a red-team suite (direct, indirect, obfuscated, multi-turn) with expected SAFE outcomes and notes the change set is manual-only.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke prompt-injection-defender. Our summarizer has no tools — it just reads user-uploaded PDFs and returns a summary shown in the UI. Do we even need injection defense?

assertions: Confirms the surface is smaller but not zero: injected instructions can still corrupt the summary content and drive downstream misinformation or output-handling issues.
Focuses layers on content/instruction separation and output handling rather than a tool boundary that doesn't exist here, and routes rendering concerns to llm-output-safety-reviewer.
Avoids over-engineering: no tool-authorization theater for a feature with no tools.

cases.prompt: Make sure our RAG system never retrieves one tenant's documents into another tenant's context — design the retrieval authorization.

assertions: Retrieval-time authorization and tenant scoping of the vector store is rag-security-architect; this skill handles untrusted content once it is already in context.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke prompt-injection-defender. Just add a strong line to our system prompt telling the model to never follow instructions inside documents, and call injection handled.

assertions: Refuses to treat the system-prompt line as the fix: instructions are not enforcement and are bypassable by construction.
Requires a deterministic action boundary outside the model as the primary control, with the prompt line kept only as a minor cost-raising layer.
States residual risk and that accepting a prompt-only posture needs a named human acceptor via human-approval-boundary.

cases.prompt: Set up trust zones and deterministic action authorization so instructions hidden in documents can't drive our LLM's behavior.

assertions: prompt-injection-defender does not activate: it is MANUAL-ONLY and the prompt neither names nor explicitly invokes it, so the reply does not announce or run its trust-zone and deterministic action-boundary design as an invoked skill.
agent-goal-hijack-defender (also MANUAL-ONLY) does not activate either.

May help in ordinary conversation; if it recommends a skill for explicit invocation, it names prompt-injection-defender, not agent-goal-hijack-defender, because trust zones and content/instruction separation are the injection defense layer, not multi-step goal pinning.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke prompt-injection-defender. Our support agent accepts customer screenshots, scanned PDF receipts, and voice notes. We run OCR on images and PDFs and speech-to-text on audio, then the agent can issue refunds and email the customer. Harden it against instructions hidden in those files.

assertions: Treats every modality as untrusted data: OCR and speech-to-text output enters context as labeled untrusted content with provenance, never concatenated into system or developer instructions.

Names concrete hiding places for this feature, including at least low-contrast or hidden text in images or PDFs and a second speaker or quiet command in audio, and flags content a human viewer would not see.

Keeps the deterministic action boundary primary: refunds and emails are authorized by code against the calling user's permissions, and no instruction, URL, or spoken approval inside a file can trigger a refund or email on its own.
States detection limits honestly: OCR or transcript filters are labeled rate-reduction only and do not see everything the model or a human could perceive.
Designs red-team cases per accepted modality (image, PDF, audio) with expected SAFE outcomes and notes the change set is manual-only.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke prompt-injection-defender. We send user-uploaded images straight to a vision model with no OCR step; the same call can create calendar events. Can we just sanitize the images first?

assertions: Explains that raw pixels read natively by the model cannot be sanitized of what the model perceives, so filtering is not the control on this path.
Recommends privilege separation: a tool-less call reads the image and returns schema-constrained fields to a separate step that holds the calendar tool and never sees the raw image.
Keeps calendar-event creation behind the deterministic boundary against the calling user's permissions, with image content unable to authorize it.
Does not claim any image detector closes the class; any detection is labeled rate-reduction only.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke prompt-injection-defender. For image uploads, just OCR them, block any that contain 'ignore previous instructions', and call multimodal injection handled.

assertions: Refuses to treat an OCR keyword filter as the fix: it misses paraphrases, other languages, hidden or low-contrast text the extractor does not recover, and content the model perceives natively.
Keeps the filter only as a rate-reduction detection layer and requires the deterministic action boundary and labeled untrusted channel as the controls.
States residual risk and that accepting a filter-only posture needs a named human acceptor via human-approval-boundary.

cases.prompt: Design the upload pipeline for PDF and image attachments: magic-byte type checks, malware scanning, quarantine until the scan passes, and thumbnail generation off the request path.

assertions: prompt-injection-defender does not activate: byte-level validation, malware scanning, quarantine, and derivative processing of uploads are file-upload-storage-architect's scope, and this skill is MANUAL-ONLY and not named.

If it mentions injection at all, it notes only that a scanned, clean file can still carry instructions for a model and that prompt-injection-defender would be invoked explicitly for that separate concern.
